introduction_markdown:
**Cameroon General Certificate of Education Board - General Certificate of Education Examination. Further Mathematics 3 (0775), ADVANCED LEVEL, June 2019. Duration: two and a half hours.**

Answer ALL questions. For your guidance the approximate mark allocation for parts of each question is indicated in brackets. Mathematical formulae and tables, published by the Board, and noiseless non-programmable electronic calculators are allowed. In calculations, you are advised to show all the steps in your working, giving your answer at each stage.

The paper contains eight questions.
enonce_intro_markdown: A particle moves round the polar curve $r = a(2+\cos\theta)$, $a>0$, with constant angular velocity $\omega$.

questions.enonce_markdown: Find, in terms of $r$, $a$ and $\omega$, the radial component of the acceleration of the particle. *[4 marks]*
questions.corrige_markdown:
In polar coordinates the radial component of acceleration is

$$a_r=\ddot r-r\dot\theta^2,\qquad \dot\theta=\omega\ \text{(constant)}.$$

From $r=a(2+\cos\theta)$:

$$\dot r=-a\sin\theta\,\dot\theta=-a\omega\sin\theta,\qquad \ddot r=-a\omega\cos\theta\,\dot\theta=-a\omega^2\cos\theta.$$

To express $\ddot r$ in terms of $r$, use $a\cos\theta=r-2a$:

$$\ddot r=-\omega^2(r-2a).$$

Then

$$a_r=-\omega^2(r-2a)-r\omega^2=-\omega^2(2r-2a)=\boxed{-2\omega^2(r-a)}.$$

(The negative sign means the radial component points towards the origin when $r>a$.)

questions.enonce_markdown: Show that the maximum magnitude of the acceleration of the particle is $4a\omega^2$, stating the angle at which this occurs. *[5 marks]*
questions.corrige_markdown:
The transverse component is $a_\theta = r\ddot\theta+2\dot r\dot\theta$. With $\dot\theta=\omega$ constant, $\ddot\theta=0$, so

$$a_\theta = 2\dot r\omega=-2a\omega^2\sin\theta.$$

From part (i), $a_r=-2\omega^2(r-a)=-2\omega^2 a(1+\cos\theta)$ (because $r-a=a(1+\cos\theta)$).

**Magnitude squared:**

$$|\mathbf{a}|^2=a_r^2+a_\theta^2=4a^2\omega^4\left[(1+\cos\theta)^2+\sin^2\theta\right]=4a^2\omega^4\left[2+2\cos\theta\right]=8a^2\omega^4(1+\cos\theta).$$

This is greatest when $\cos\theta=1$, that is $\theta=0$ (or $2n\pi$), where $r=3a$:

$$|\mathbf{a}|^2_{\max}=16a^2\omega^4\quad\Longrightarrow\quad |\mathbf{a}|_{\max}=\boxed{4a\omega^2}.$$

It occurs at $\theta=0$ (and every $\theta=2n\pi$), the point of the curve furthest from the origin, where the acceleration is purely radial, directed towards the origin.
